evidence: A new GitHub Actions workflow makes 8 artificial SQLite rows in a producer runner and packs them into source-free SHA256 verified parts, uploads the bundle via actions/upload-artifact@v4, and independently downloads and verifies it in a different runner. Offline contract tests reject tampering, missing pieces, forged durability claims, and budget inflation. The initial PR branch's two-job synthetic roundtrip passed in run 37945062113; exact final HEAD must be revalidated.
limitations: Synthetic artifact transport proves neither Kaggle-authenticated external upload nor persistence after Kaggle interruption.
A seven-day Actions artifact is temporary, not a verified long-term GitHub Release backup or Kaggle resumability.
No real sAlex/WBM/MPTrj bytes, model training claims or large Kaggle job are used.
